image_description: A European fire salamander (Salamandra salamandra) is shown from a high-angle view, resting on a textured, mossy rock surface. The salamander has a glossy black body with vivid yellow spots and bands. Its head is broad and flattened, with visible parotoid glands behind the eyes. The eyes are small, dark, and protruding. The body is robust and cylindrical, with short, stout limbs. The forelimbs have four digits, and the hindlimbs have five digits, all blunt and unwebbed. The tail is laterally compressed, shorter than the body length, and has a rounded tip. The skin appears smooth, moist, and glandular, with a glossy, wet-looking appearance.
